newsitem.title: FRANCE: CADES planning to issue in francs again - dealers.
newsitem.headline: CADES planning to issue in francs again - dealers.

text.p: French welfare debt repayment fund CADES is looking to issue up to 18 billion francs of bonds, possibly as soon as next week, syndication managers said on Friday.

Dealers in Paris said at the moment there were no firm details, but most said they expected CADES to sell about 10 billion francs of a new 2005 bond and to add to either of its existing franc bonds maturing in 2002 and 2007.

A source close to the CADES confirmed the fund was looking at the franc market but declined to give any details. "Bearing in mind the market's bullish, why not? But nothing has been decided yet, neither timing, maturity or amount," the source said on Friday.

Syndication managers said next week offered a good window of opportunity for the fund to issue bonds, partly because there were no government OAT or BTAN auctions. Regular government bond auctions take place in each of the following three weeks, two in francs and one in Ecu.
They also said that apart from the market sensitive Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday, next week would be relatively quiet for bond markets.
"Next week is the best window for several weeks, it's by no means far-fetched," said one syndication manager at a French bank.
Others said domestic investors had surplus cash at the moment and pointed out that there would be a total of 110 billion francs of redemptions and coupon payments on government bonds in October.
Of the two existing bonds, dealers said the CADES fund would be more likely to favour the 2002 bond than the 2007.
"It's trading quite well at the moment and I would expect more to come," said one syndication manager at a French bank.
Another said he thought the total would be between 15-18 billion francs including 10 billion in 2005 bonds, the remainder being made up with sales of both the 2002 and 2007 bonds.
A third syndication manager said CADES would probably issue a new 2005 bond to broaden its maturity range, and avoid building up a few large issues.
"There wouldn't be any problem with the 2002 because it's a little expensive. There would also be demand for the 2007 but I don't think CADES wants to have 30 billion of each line," he said.
He added that as CADES already has franc bonds maturing in 2002 and 2007 and guilder bonds maturing in 2004, a 2005 franc bond would leave gaps at the three, five and ten year area of the curve.
He said the fund could be reserving these maturities for a mark or dollar issue which was widely expected some time before the end of the year.
CADES president Benoit Jolivet said in July the fund was planning more operations in the autumn and besides francs was still considering issuing bonds in dollars, Ecu, marks, guilders or yen.
